findings.title: A COLUMN-level grant to a role anon inherits escapes BOTH arms of the privilege guard
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Not equivalent and not on an unexecuted branch: both arms run and both return zero rows while anon really can read the outbox payload. Measured on the clone at HEAD: relacl stayed {test=arwdDxt/test} (Arm A table half sees nothing), attacl became payload={rt_probe=r/test} (Arm A column half filters on grantee = 0 OR grantee::regrole::text IN ('anon','authenticated'), and rt_probe is neither), has_table_privilege('anon','public.job_outbox','SELECT') = f (Arm B asks a TABLE-level question, which a column grant does not answer), has_column_privilege('anon','public.job_outbox','payload','SELECT') = t, pg_has_role('anon','rt_probe','USAGE') = t. The inheritance leg is live in every environment: anon and authenticated carry rolinherit = true on the local container (PostgreSQL 16.14) and on BOTH Supabase projects (17.0006, introspected read-only 2026-09-07). This is the direct successor of RT-7: round 2 closed the PUBLIC leg in Arm A and the table-level MEMBERSHIP leg in Arm B, and the intersection of the two — column AND membership — is covered by neither. The suite header positively claims the opposite at lines 30-34 ('who is NAMED in the ACL, table and column') and 40-41 ('Arm B also catches a grant reaching anon through role MEMBERSHIP'). Suggested closure: give Arm B a has_column_privilege leg over pg_attribute, or resolve membership in Arm A's column half with pg_has_role(client_role, acl.grantee, 'USAGE') instead of a name/0 filter.

findings.title: The tagged dollar-quote + concatenated-token construct defeats both text checks; in the REVOKE direction nothing else catches it
findings.arbiter_reasoning: MUT-02 and MUT-03 both survived title 2. The construct is DO $tag$ BEGIN EXECUTE 'REVO' || 'KE ...'; END $tag$; — three properties compose: the statement parser's /\$\$[\s\S]*?\$\$/ mask does not handle a TAGGED dollar-quote, so the block splits at its inner semicolon into fragments starting DO and END and never matches ^REVOKE/^GRANT; D17's belt counts \bREVOKE\b, and 'REVO' || 'KE carries no such token, so the count stays 1; \bGRANT\b stays null. The two directions are NOT symmetric. MUT-03 (re-GRANT to anon) is backstopped by title 4 Arm A once the migration is applied — MUT-09 proves Arm A kills a direct named grant — which matches RT-9's accepted disposition. MUT-02 (widened REVOKE against service_role or the owner) has NO backstop: grep of the suite returns ZERO non-comment assertions naming service_role or the owner, an omission lines 61-70 record deliberately and then claim is covered — 'both are guarded by title 3's exact-match statement assertion instead of by an assertion that could only be true by accident'. MUT-02 falsifies that sentence, and D17/RT-9's closing argument ('only the catalogue bounds what it DOES') cannot transfer to a role the catalogue arm never asks about. P0 on D18's own recorded reasoning for RT-7: a confirmed, executed, provably non-equivalent survivor with no other detector, plus a positively false claim in the artifact's own header.

findings.title: The three forbidden-form guards match raw text with literal single spaces, so a newline inside the keyword phrase evades them
findings.arbiter_reasoning:
MUT-04 and MUT-05 both survived title 3. /CREATE POLICY/i, /FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY/i and /DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY/i (and the positive /ALTER TABLE job_outbox ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;/) are matched against the RAW file with literal single spaces. PostgreSQL accepts a newline or a run of spaces anywhere between those keywords, so 'ALTER TABLE job_outbox
  DISABLE ROW LEVEL
  SECURITY;' and 'CREATE
  POLICY job_outbox_client_read ON job_outbox FOR SELECT TO anon USING (true);' are valid SQL that no check sees. The comment at 176-178 argues for raw text because the statement parser masks the DO body, without noticing that the statement list ALREADY collapses whitespace at line 114 — the fixes for D9 and RT-8 landed separately and gave up, between them, the one normalisation that would have closed this. Neither mutant is equivalent and both branches execute. Graded P0: RT-8 closed exactly this statement with a literal regex and it is re-opened in a new spelling, and lines 47-49 call the file-text case 'the ONLY environment-independent guard'. Mitigation, measured rather than assumed: MUT-06 shows title 1 kills a DISABLE once the file is applied and MUT-07 shows title 1 kills an added policy, so a container at head does catch both consequences — but the guard the file names as the environment-independent one does not. Closure: run the three checks over topLevelStatements() as well, or spell them with \s+ (in-repo precedent: migration-045-onboarding-demos-rls.test.ts:12, migration-043-structure.test.ts:47).

findings.title: Arm B fails OPEN when its derived privilege list is empty, and nothing asserts the list is non-empty
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Measured on the container: acldefault('r', NULL) IS NULL and aclexplode(NULL) returns 0 rows, so an empty server_privileges CTE makes the CROSS JOIN empty and expect(effective).toEqual([]) pass vacuously. Currently UNREACHABLE — 'public.job_outbox'::regclass raises rather than returning NULL when the table is absent, and Arm A executes first — so this is latent, not live, hence P2. It is still a security oracle with no self-check. One line closes it: assert the derived list has 7 types on PostgreSQL 16 and 8 on 17 (measured this pass: 7 locally, 8 incl. MAINTAIN on both Supabase projects). Also verified sound: the CTE is indifferent to relowner changing (ALTER TABLE job_outbox OWNER TO anon still derives 7 types, and both arms then fire because the owner change rewrites relacl).
